name: HTTP

hero.title: Your API sent { id: 7 }. Your client called it a User.
hero.lede: `@pyreon/http` is a `fetch` client that checks what comes back against your schema, times out by default, encodes path params for you and keeps errors typed. Retries, auth and mocks are plain middleware, and the core has zero dependencies.

facts.value: zero dependencies<small>Middleware, schemas, streams and SSR live in their own entries.</small>
on, 30 s<small>`fetch` has none; a hung server never settles the promise.</small>
any Standard Schema<small>Zod, Valibot, ArkType, `s`, or a plain `(raw) => T`.</small>
{dot:warn}endpoints on iOS and Android<small>Experimental; `useFetch` / `useQuery` over an endpoint lower to native networking.</small>

items.title: Responses are checked, not cast
items.text: Declare `response: User` once and every call is validated. A payload that drifts throws `ResponseValidationError` at the boundary instead of crashing a component three screens later. Set `validate: 'warn'` to log and degrade instead.

items.title: Middleware, not interceptors
items.text: `(request, next) => response`. Retry calls `next()` in a loop, refresh re-issues after a 401, a mock returns without calling `next`. No `__isRetry` flags, no `eject()` handles, order is the `use` array.

items.title: One declaration, three uses
items.text: `api.endpoint('GET /users/:id', { response: User })` is a typed function, a `.query()` for `useQuery` with its cache key, and a `.mutation()`. `params` is required exactly when the path has placeholders.

items.title: Safe on a busy server
items.text: Clients are immutable (`extend()` derives), and `runWithRequest` keeps each SSR render's request in `AsyncLocalStorage`, so one user's cookie can't reach another user's render. `forwardHeaders` needs an allowlist and stops at your origin.

difference.title: Everything the bare `fetch` call quietly skips.

before.label: fetch, by hand
before.caption: A timer for the timeout, string-built URLs, a status check, and a cast that believes anything.

after.label: with @pyreon/http
after.caption: Timeout on, params encoded, retry and auth as middleware, the body validated.

demo.title: Send a request through the middleware.
demo.text: Send a request through real middleware into a mock server. Make the server fail and watch `retry()` back off; make it hang and the default timeout end it with a `TimeoutError`; make it return the wrong shape and see `ResponseValidationError` before your UI does.
demo.referenceHtml:
server
use: [bearer(…), retry({ limit: 2 })]
timeout: 10_000  // default, shortened here
request log
demo.spec: DemoHttp uses the real `createHttp` with `retry({ limit: 2 })` and `@pyreon/http/mock` as the transport, so no network is used. Server modes: ok; fail once with 503 (retry succeeds on attempt 2); always 503 (`ServerError` after 3 attempts); hang (the demo lowers `timeout` to 3 s so the `TimeoutError` arrives quickly, and says so); wrong shape (`{ id: 7 }` → `ResponseValidationError`). Each attempt is logged with its delay.

items.name: `createHttp` + `extend()`
items.text: immutable clients; `extend` adds headers and middleware and leaves the parent alone.

items.name: Three validation tiers
items.text: `.json<User>()` cast, `.json(isUser)` guard, `.json(UserSchema)` with any Standard Schema.

items.name: Error bodies by status
items.text: `errors: { 404: NotFound, '5XX': Outage }` validates and types the failure body.

items.name: Streams
items.text: `openEventStream` (SSE with resume and backoff) and `openNdjsonStream`, over POST, with auth and mocks.

items.name: Mocks without MSW
items.text: `createMock` is middleware; unmatched requests fall through to the real transport.

items.name: Native middleware
items.text: `bearer`, `retry` and `logger` in a literal `use` array lower to iOS and Android with web semantics. Experimental.

api.title: A small core and opt-in entries.

limits.title: No cache, on purpose
limits.text: Caching, dedup and retries-by-default belong to `@pyreon/query`, which calls this client. Retry here is opt-in so the two don't multiply.

limits.title: Use `params`, never a template string
limits.text: Building the path with a template string skips encoding, so an id of `../admin` reaches `/admin`. Write `api.get('/users/:id', { params: { id } })`; the `pyreon/no-unencoded-path-interpolation` lint rule flags the other form.

limits.title: Bearer tokens stay on your origin
limits.text: `bearer` and `forwardHeaders` only attach to requests on `baseUrl`'s origin unless you pass `{ crossOrigin: true }`.

limits.title: `.mutation()` and strict optional types
limits.text: Today `useMutation(endpoint.mutation({ invalidates }))` fails to typecheck with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (on in Pyreon's preset). Pass `{ mutationFn, invalidates: [endpoint.key.prefix] }` instead, as in the recipe below.

related.name: Query

related.name: Auth
related.text: `bearer` plus `refresh` keep an OIDC session's token current. Auth lands in the next release.

end.title: Trust the network a little less. Your types a little more.

default timeout on every request; retry stays off so Query's 3 retries don't become 16 requests.
shared scenarios that the web middleware and the iOS and Android runtimes must answer identically (next release, experimental).

comingFrom.title: Interceptors become middleware; the cast becomes a check.
comingFrom.note: axios has no retry by default, so a 503 throws, and a `{ id: 7 }` body comes back typed as a `User`. The Pyreon client retries the 503 and throws `ResponseValidationError` on the bad body.

comingFrom.title: Same fetch-first idea, plus endpoints and schemas.
comingFrom.note: ky already retries and times out by default. What you gain: `params` encoding from the path, a declared response schema, typed error bodies, and one endpoint that also feeds `useQuery`.

comingFrom.title: Keep the defaults you like, add a schema.
comingFrom.note: ofetch's `onRequest` hook becomes `bearer()`. The response is validated instead of cast, and an abort stays an `AbortError`, separate from real failures.

recipes.title: Tests with no network and no MSW
recipes.text: A mock is middleware, so it can't leak between test files, and unmatched routes fall through.

recipes.title: Stream an LLM reply over POST
recipes.text: `EventSource` can't POST, send auth or be mocked. `openEventStream` can, and `break` closes the connection.

recipes.title: A todo list where URL, key and type can't drift
recipes.text: Endpoints feed `useQuery` directly, and a mutation invalidates every query of the list endpoint.

faq.a: The record has a head-to-head with ofetch, ky, redaxios and axios, but its harness changed after that run (a new 'library defaults' row, PR #4142), so we are not quoting it here until the next measured run. The `bench/` file is in the repo.

Because `@pyreon/query` already retries three times, so a failing query makes four attempts. A client that also retried three times would send four requests per attempt: sixteen in all. Add `retry()` where you call the client directly.

faq.q: Does it run on the server?
faq.a: Yes, on Node, Bun and edge runtimes with `fetch`. `@pyreon/http/server` is the only entry that touches `node:async_hooks`, so it never lands in a browser bundle.

The imperative client is web and server. Same-file endpoints called through `useFetch` or `useQuery` lower to the native networking runtime, and `bearer`, `retry` and `logger` middleware cross too (next release). Native is experimental.
